title: Antisemitism and Free Speech Collide on Campuses

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: The story behind a congressional hearing that ended the career of one university president, jeopardized the jobs of two others,
sentences.zh: 一场国会听证会背后的故事，它终结了一位大学校长的职业生涯，危及了另外两位的职位，

sentences.en: and kicked off an emotional debate about anti-Semitism and free speech on college campuses.
sentences.zh: 并引发了一场关于大学校园内反犹太主义和言论自由的激烈辩论。

sentences.en: I speak with my colleague, Nick Confessori.
sentences.zh: 我将与我的同事尼克·孔费索里进行对话。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 今天是星期三。

sentences.en: December 13th.
Nick, thank you for coming in here.
sentences.zh: 尼克，谢谢你来到这里。

sentences.en: It's good to be here, Michael.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I want you to give us the backstory that brings us to this now infamous congressional hearing last week featuring several of the country's top college presidents.
sentences.zh: 我想请你为我们梳理一下背景，带我们了解上周那场备受争议的国会听证会，当时几位全国顶尖的大学校长出席了会议。

sentences.en: And to the uproar that this hearing ultimately ends up triggering, where does that story start?
sentences.zh: 以及这场听证会最终引发的轩然大波，这个故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: It begins in the aftermath of the October 7th attacks, when around the country, campuses begin to be roiled by protests about the attacks, the aftermath of the attacks,
sentences.zh: 故事始于10月7日袭击事件之后，当时全国各地的校园开始被关于袭击事件、袭击后果的抗议活动所搅动，

sentences.en: the Israeli response.
sentences.zh: 以及以色列的回应。

sentences.en: You had students chanting from the river to the sea, Palestine will be free, which for some of the protesters were meant as more generic statements of Palestinian freedom.
sentences.zh: 学生们高喊“从河流到海洋，巴勒斯坦将获得自由”，对于一些抗议者来说，这被视为对巴勒斯坦自由更普遍的诉求。

sentences.en: But for many Jews, sound like calls for ethnic cleansing of Jews from Israel.
sentences.zh: 但对许多犹太人来说，这听起来像是呼吁将犹太人从以色列进行种族清洗。

sentences.en: Because between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea is Israel and its current borders.
sentences.zh: 因为约旦河和地中海之间就是以色列及其目前的边界。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You had chants intifada, intifada.
sentences.zh: 还有人高喊“起义，起义”。

sentences.en: Long live the intifada, which is a word that means uprising, but which many people, especially people of a certain age,
sentences.zh: “起义万岁”，这个词的意思是反抗，但对许多人，尤其是特定年龄段的人来说，

sentences.en: sounds like an endorsement of the violent tactics of the second intifada, suicide attacks.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是对第二次起义中暴力策略和自杀式袭击的支持。

sentences.en: And at least some of these events, I remember feeling so empowered, that victory was near and so tangible.
sentences.zh: 至少在其中一些活动中，我记得感到非常振奋，胜利近在咫尺，触手可及。

sentences.en: You could hear speakers who were praising the attacks of October 7th.
sentences.zh: 你可以听到演讲者在赞美10月7日的袭击。

sentences.en: It was exhilarating.
sentences.zh: 那令人振奋。

sentences.en: It was exhilarating.
sentences.zh: 那令人振奋。

sentences.en: It was energizing.
sentences.zh: 那让人充满活力。

sentences.en: Endorsing them, celebrating them.
sentences.zh: 支持他们，庆祝他们。

sentences.en: And there was one vivid example at UCLA, where students battered a piñata of Benjamin Netanyahu, the prime minister of Israel, while a woman chanted,
sentences.zh: 加州大学洛杉矶分校有一个生动的例子，学生们殴打一个以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡的皮纳塔（玩偶），同时一名女子高喊：

sentences.en: Beat that Jew.
sentences.zh: “打那个犹太人。”

sentences.en: A lot of those moments were seen by millions of people who wouldn't otherwise tune in to what's happening on these campuses.
sentences.zh: 许多原本不会关注这些校园动态的人，通过视频看到了这些时刻。

sentences.en: And for Jews on these campuses, these videos and images often made them feel unsafe, even if they weren't intended that way by the students.
sentences.zh: 对于这些校园里的犹太人来说，这些视频和图像往往让他们感到不安全，即使学生们并非有意为之。

sentences.en: On top of that, donors and alumni are seeing them.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，捐赠者和校友们也看到了这些。

sentences.en: They're getting really, really upset.
sentences.zh: 他们感到非常、非常愤怒。

sentences.en: And they start making calls, and they start to write emails.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始打电话，开始写邮件。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And those calls and those emails basically say, what?
sentences.zh: 而那些电话和邮件基本上说了些什么？

sentences.en: Almost from the beginning, you were hearing from donors and alumni who felt that the response of these college presidents was not forceful enough.
sentences.zh: 几乎从一开始，你就能听到捐赠者和校友们的声音，他们认为这些大学校长的回应不够有力。

sentences.en: They wanted a real intervention.
sentences.zh: 他们想要真正的干预。

sentences.en: And they wanted powerful statements that the behavior they were seeing on these videos was not okay, was not accepted at these institutions.
sentences.zh: 他们想要强有力的声明，表明他们在视频中看到的行为是不对的，在这些机构中是不可接受的。

sentences.en: And so against that backdrop, Republicans in the House of Representatives decide that they're going to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这样的背景下，众议院的共和党人决定采取行动。

sentences.en: They're going to hold a hearing on campus anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 他们要举行一场关于校园反犹太主义的听证会。

sentences.en: And they invite the presidents of three universities.
sentences.zh: 他们邀请了三所大学的校长。

sentences.en: Elizabeth McGill from the University of Pennsylvania, Claudine Gay from Harvard, and Sally Kornbluth from MIT.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学的伊丽莎白·麦吉尔、哈佛大学的克劳丁·盖伊，以及麻省理工学院的萨莉·科恩布鲁斯。

sentences.en: And why did the Republicans invite these three university presidents of all the university presidents in the country?
sentences.zh: 为什么共和党人要在全国众多的大学校长中邀请这三位？

sentences.en: It's not entirely clear why they picked these three schools.
sentences.zh: 目前还不完全清楚他们为什么选择这三所学校。

sentences.en: In fact, there have been incidents like this at lower-profile schools all around the country.
sentences.zh: 事实上，全国各地知名度较低的学校也发生过类似事件。

sentences.en: But what they all have in common is that they are high-profile institutions.
sentences.zh: 但它们的共同点是，它们都是高知名度的机构。

sentences.en: They are considered the elite of academia.
sentences.zh: 它们被认为是学术界的精英。

sentences.en: And making it about them makes it a really big story.
sentences.zh: 把焦点对准它们，让这成了一个非常重大的新闻。

sentences.en: And heading into this hearing, what exactly were these congressional Republicans up to?
sentences.zh: 在听证会开始前，这些国会共和党人到底想干什么？

sentences.en: What are their aims for getting these three prestigious college presidents before them?
sentences.zh: 他们让这三位名校校长出席听证会的目的是什么？

sentences.en: Well, if you pull back a little bit, think how over the last couple of years,
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你退后一步，想想过去几年里，

sentences.en: Republicans and conservatives have tried to make the case that there is something seriously wrong in academia.
sentences.zh: 共和党人和保守派一直试图证明学术界存在严重问题。

sentences.en: And that they need to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们需要对此采取行动。

sentences.en: And for many months this year, this was at the center of the Republican primary for president.
sentences.zh: 今年有好几个月，这都是共和党总统初选的核心议题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Attacks on, quote-unquote, wokeism.
sentences.zh: 对所谓的“觉醒文化”的攻击。

sentences.en: Attacks on critical race theory.
sentences.zh: 对批判性种族理论的攻击。

sentences.en: An overemphasis on race and oppression.
sentences.zh: 对种族和压迫的过度强调。

sentences.en: And in their minds and in their argument, those ideas are at the heart of what we saw on those campuses.
sentences.zh: 在他们的想法和论点中，这些思想正是我们在校园里所见现象的核心。

sentences.en: And they saw an opportunity to make that case and make that point to the American public.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了一个机会，可以向美国公众阐明这一观点。

sentences.en: After a few months in which it seemed that a lot of voters in particular had stopped tuning into those arguments.
sentences.zh: 此前几个月，似乎很多选民已经不再关注这些论点了。

sentences.en: So they're going to try to make a direct link between this liberal culture on college campuses,
sentences.zh: 所以他们试图在大学校园里的这种自由派文化，

sentences.en: which they've been denouncing, and this anti-Israeli rhetoric they're seeing on campuses.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们一直谴责的东西，与他们在校园里看到的这种反以色列言论之间建立直接联系。

sentences.en: They're going to suggest that those two things are inextricably bound up together.
sentences.zh: 他们暗示这两者是密不可分的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So how does the hearing actually start?
sentences.zh: 那么听证会实际上是怎么开始的？

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: The Committee on Education and Workforce will come to order.
sentences.zh: 教育与劳动力委员会现在开会。

sentences.en: So the way it begins, and the part you didn't see on the newscasts that night, was each of the college presidents...
sentences.zh: 会议开始的方式，以及那天你在新闻报道中没看到的部分，是每位大学校长……

sentences.en: We at Harvard reject anti-Semitism and denounce any trace of it on our campus or within our community.
sentences.zh: “我们在哈佛拒绝反犹太主义，并谴责校园内或社区内任何形式的反犹太主义。”

sentences.en: Forcefully denouncing anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 有力地谴责反犹太主义。

sentences.en: Let me reiterate my and Penn's unyielding commitment to combating it.
sentences.zh: “让我重申我和宾大在打击反犹太主义方面坚定不移的承诺。”

sentences.en: Saying that this kind of rhetoric is hurtful.
sentences.zh: 表示这种言论是有害的。

sentences.en: We have increased security measures, expanded reporting channels, and augmented counseling, mental health, and support services.
sentences.zh: “我们加强了安保措施，扩大了举报渠道，并增加了咨询、心理健康和支持服务。”

sentences.en: Here are the steps we are taking to combat anti-Semitism on our campuses.
sentences.zh: 这是我们为打击校园反犹太主义所采取的措施。

sentences.en: I must, at the same time, ensure that we protect speech and viewpoint diversity for everyone.
sentences.zh: “与此同时，我必须确保我们保护每个人的言论和观点多样性。”

sentences.en: But we also have to protect free speech on campus and allow people to say things, even when we find them objectionable.
sentences.zh: 但我们也必须保护校园言论自由，允许人们表达观点，即使我们认为这些观点令人反感。

sentences.en: We need both safety and free expression for universities and ultimately democracy to thrive.
sentences.zh: 我们需要安全和言论自由，才能让大学乃至民主制度蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: And they were trying to set up this idea that people are going to say things you don't agree with, even terrible things you don't agree with.
sentences.zh: 他们试图建立这样一个理念：人们会说出你不同意的观点，甚至是令人反感的糟糕言论。

sentences.en: And the values of our university can be thought of as separate from the speech that we allow as an academic institution.
sentences.zh: 而我们大学的价值观可以被视为与我们作为学术机构所允许的言论是分开的。

sentences.en: And they seem to want to distinguish between free speech and harassment.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎想在言论自由和骚扰之间做出区分。

sentences.en: I watched the hearing.
sentences.zh: 我看了听证会。

sentences.en: They're trying to say some free speech is just free speech.
sentences.zh: 他们试图说，有些言论自由仅仅是言论自由。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's harassment, but that's a really important distinction.
sentences.zh: 有时这构成了骚扰，但这确实是一个非常重要的区别。

sentences.en: That speech that incites violence is unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 煽动暴力的言论是不可接受的。

sentences.en: Yes, what they're trying to say is, when do we take action against a student as an institution for something they say?
sentences.zh: 是的，他们试图表达的是，作为机构，我们何时应该因为学生的言论而对他们采取行动？

sentences.en: Well, it has to cross a certain threshold.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它必须跨越一定的门槛。

sentences.en: It has to be pervasive.
sentences.zh: 它必须是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: It has to be harassment.
sentences.zh: 它必须构成骚扰。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They were saying what is actually true under the law.
sentences.zh: 他们所说的是法律规定的事实。

sentences.en: They were expressing how things should work on these campuses.
sentences.zh: 他们表达的是这些校园应该如何运作。

sentences.en: And the problem for these presidents is that that is not how it actually works on these campuses.
sentences.zh: 而这些校长的问题在于，这些校园的实际运作方式并非如此。

sentences.en: And that is where the Republicans went next.
sentences.zh: 而这正是共和党人接下来的切入点。

sentences.en: Okay, explain that.
sentences.zh: 好的，解释一下。

sentences.en: Recognize Mr. Banks.
sentences.zh: 请班克斯议员发言。

sentences.en: So if you focus on Penn for a second, we saw in the questioning people like Congressman Jim Banks.
sentences.zh: 如果你关注宾大，我们看到了像吉姆·班克斯众议员这样的质询者。

sentences.en: And for the past year, your administration has sought to punish Amy Wax.
sentences.zh: “在过去的一年里，你们的管理层一直试图惩罚艾米·瓦克斯。”

sentences.en: Begin to float examples of conservative speakers who had been heckled or shut down or disfavored in some way on some of these college campuses.
sentences.zh: 开始列举一些在这些大学校园里被起哄、被叫停或受到某种歧视的保守派演讲者的例子。

sentences.en: He talked about how the university is currently trying to sanction Amy Wax, a law professor, her stance on DEI and identity issues.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了大学目前正试图制裁法学教授艾米·瓦克斯，因为她在DEI（多元、公平、包容）和身份问题上的立场。

sentences.en: For comments she made about the performance of black students in her classes.
sentences.zh: 因为她对班上黑人学生表现的评论。

sentences.en: And then you canceled an event with former ICE director Tom Holman due to disruptive...
sentences.zh: “然后你们取消了前ICE（移民及海关执法局）局长汤姆·霍尔曼的活动，因为破坏性的……”

sentences.en: And he said a few years ago, a Trump administration immigration official tried to come and speak at Penn.
sentences.zh: 他说几年前，一位特朗普政府的移民官员试图来宾大演讲。

sentences.en: And students there basically shut down the speech because they felt that he was bringing anti-immigration and a nativist rhetoric to campus.
sentences.zh: 那里的学生基本上叫停了演讲，因为他们认为他把反移民和本土主义的言论带到了校园。

sentences.en: On the other hand, there are examples where Penn seemed to act less decisively.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，宾大在某些情况下似乎行动不够果断。

sentences.en: Penn hosted a Palestine rights literature festival.
sentences.zh: 宾大举办了一个巴勒斯坦权利文学节。

sentences.en: For example, this fall, before the October 7th attacks, Penn played host to a Palestinian literary festival.
sentences.zh: 例如，今年秋天，在10月7日袭击事件之前，宾大举办了一个巴勒斯坦文学节。

sentences.en: Where speakers included Roger Waters, who's the former Pink Floyd front man.
sentences.zh: 演讲者包括前平克·弗洛伊德乐队主唱罗杰·沃特斯。

sentences.en: The same Roger Waters, by the way, who's publicly used anti-Jewish slurs and has dressed up as a Nazi and floated a pig balloon with the Star of David at most,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，就是那位罗杰·沃特斯，他曾公开使用反犹太人的侮辱性词汇，打扮成纳粹，并在他的大多数演唱会上，

sentences.en: at many of his concerts.
sentences.zh: 在许多演唱会上，放飞了一个带有大卫之星的猪形气球。

sentences.en: And in fact, Penn did issue a statement saying, you find some of the rhetoric objectionable.
sentences.zh: 事实上，宾大确实发表了一份声明说，你们认为某些言论令人反感。

sentences.en: It's not consistent with our values, but they're allowed to have this event.
sentences.zh: 这不符合我们的价值观，但他们被允许举办这个活动。

sentences.en: So, I think in the eyes of Republicans, one event is allowed to go ahead and the other is essentially canceled.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为在共和党人眼中，一个活动被允许进行，而另一个却被取消了。

sentences.en: And so they see that these standards are not really being applied evenly.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这些标准并没有得到公平的应用。

sentences.en: And the way that they're not being applied evenly, according to this Republican congressman, is that when Republican speakers, conservative-minded guests are coming to campus,
sentences.zh: 根据这位共和党众议员的说法，这种不公平的应用方式是：当共和党演讲者、保守派嘉宾来到校园时，

sentences.en: there's a willingness to shut things down, to quiet it.
sentences.zh: 学校愿意叫停活动，让其安静下来。

sentences.en: But when it's more liberal-minded speakers, like this pro-Palestinian speaker, greater allowances are made.
sentences.zh: 但当涉及到更倾向自由派的演讲者，比如这位亲巴勒斯坦的演讲者时，学校则给予了更大的宽容。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's what the Republicans are claiming.
sentences.zh: 这就是共和党人的主张。

sentences.en: And here's why this moment is so powerful, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，这就是为什么这一刻如此有力的原因。

sentences.en: There just aren't that many conservatives on these campuses anymore.
sentences.zh: 这些校园里已经没有那么多保守派了。

sentences.en: The student bodies tend to be pretty liberal.
sentences.zh: 学生群体往往非常自由派。

sentences.en: And the professors tend to be very liberal in terms of their distribution of political affiliation.
sentences.zh: 而教授们在政治倾向的分布上也往往非常自由派。

sentences.en: It's mostly Democrats and liberals, not Republicans and conservatives.
sentences.zh: 主要是民主党人和自由派，而不是共和党人和保守派。

sentences.en: So, when speech happens that annoys conservatives on these campuses, there aren't protests.
sentences.zh: 所以，当校园里出现让保守派感到恼火的言论时，并没有抗议活动。

sentences.en: There aren't real efforts to shut them down.
sentences.zh: 没有真正的努力去阻止他们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there are a lot of Jewish people on these campuses.
sentences.zh: 但这些校园里有很多犹太人。

sentences.en: And one of the things that made this moment so powerful and important and useful politically on the Republican side was that they could really put the shoe on the other foot in a way that would appeal to an audience much broader than liberals who care on principle about free speech.
sentences.zh: 这一时刻之所以如此有力、重要且在共和党方面具有政治价值，原因之一在于他们能够以一种吸引比那些原则上关心言论自由的自由派更广泛受众的方式，将矛头反转。

sentences.zh: 斯特凡尼克不断追问，呼吁对犹太人进行种族灭绝，换句话说，仅仅因为他们是犹太人就杀光他们，这是否构成欺凌或骚扰？

sentences.en: So, the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 所以，答案是肯定的。

sentences.zh: 这是一个取决于具体情况的决定，国会议员女士。

sentences.zh: 而麦吉尔一直用这种官僚式的语言回答。

sentences.zh: 是的，麦吉尔女士。

sentences.zh: 如果你是在讨论如何管理和规范校园言论的背景下谈论这个问题，那可能是一个恰当的回答。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.

sentences.zh: 而这正是让这一刻对他们造成如此大损害的原因。

sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，在这次听证会之后，在所有要求辞职的呼声中，宾大、麻省理工和哈佛这三位大学校长会怎样？

sentences.en: The fallout comes very swiftly.
sentences.zh: 后果来得非常迅速。

sentences.zh: 几天之内，70名国会议员呼吁这三位校长全部辞职。

sentences.en: And in some ways, the most pressure is on Liz McGill, president of UPenn, where the donors and the school's board members are the most outspoken and active at this moment.

sentences.en: She talks about essentially being too legalistic and not speaking clearly enough on this important question of whether genocide is okay.

sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，这些众议院共和党人，似乎以斯特凡尼克议员为代表，尼克，你曾为《时报》写过很多关于她的文章，

sentences.en: that there was a petition calling for her ouster from the board.
sentences.zh: 以至于有人请愿要求将她逐出董事会。

sentences.en: I remember this now.
sentences.zh: 我现在想起来了。

sentences.en: And she was pushed off of the board of an institution she had once loved and been groomed for her political career.
sentences.zh: 她被赶出了一个她曾经热爱并为之培养了政治生涯的机构的董事会。

sentences.en: So, she's pushed out of a position she loved at Harvard, basically because she lied about the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 所以，她被赶出了她在哈佛热爱的职位，基本上是因为她在2020年大选问题上撒了谎。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And when she was pushed out, she put out this defiant statement, saying that Harvard had decided to, quote, cave to the woke left,
sentences.zh: 当她被赶走时，她发表了一份挑衅性的声明，称哈佛已经决定，引用她的话，“向觉醒派左翼屈服”，

sentences.en: and that she would wear being kicked off the board as a, quote, badge of honor.
sentences.zh: 并表示她会把被踢出董事会视为一种“荣誉勋章”。

sentences.en: And you begin to sense that there is more at play here than just this rhetoric about openness and dialogue.
sentences.zh: 你开始感觉到，这里涉及的不仅仅是关于开放和对话的言论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Her motivations here, especially in going after a place like Harvard that, in her mind, has done her wrong, they're messy.
sentences.zh: 她在这里的动机，特别是在针对像哈佛这样一个在她看来亏待过她的地方时，是非常混乱的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think Stefanik is also an example of a broader problem that Republicans have been wrestling with in their coalition,
sentences.zh: 我认为斯特凡尼克也是共和党人在其联盟中一直努力解决的一个更广泛问题的例子，

sentences.en: which is anti-Semitic and nativist ideas among some of their supporters.
sentences.zh: 那就是在他们的一些支持者中存在反犹太主义和本土主义思想。

sentences.en: Okay, explain that.
sentences.zh: 好的，解释一下。

sentences.en: In recent years, what was once a fringe ideology of the very far right, something called Great Replacement Theory, has crept into the Republican mainstream.
sentences.zh: 近年来，曾经属于极右翼边缘意识形态的所谓“大置换理论”（Great Replacement Theory），已经渗透到了共和党的主流中。

sentences.en: And the most extreme version of this theory is that there is a conspiracy of global elites to turn white civilizations and countries into brown ones through immigration.
sentences.zh: 这种理论最极端的版本是，存在一个全球精英阴谋，通过移民将白人文明和国家变成棕色人种国家。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And often in the most extreme versions of this, the Jews are pulling the strings.
sentences.zh: 在最极端的版本中，通常是犹太人在幕后操纵。

sentences.en: The Jews are part of a conspiracy to undermine Western civilization by replacing white Americans or white Europeans with immigrants from Africa, from Asia, from the Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 犹太人是破坏西方文明阴谋的一部分，他们通过用来自非洲、亚洲、中东的移民来取代美国或欧洲的白人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We've talked about this on the show.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: It's seen as responsible for some of the anti-Semitic violence on the American right.
sentences.zh: 它被视为美国右翼一些反犹太暴力事件的罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in fact, we've had three mass shootings in recent years in this country where the shooters wrote about replacement theory, seemed to be inspired by replacement theory.
sentences.zh: 事实上，近年来在这个国家发生了三起大规模枪击事件，枪手都写过关于置换理论的内容，似乎受到了置换理论的启发。

sentences.en: The most popular cable host in the country up until this year, Tucker Carlson, was also one of the great popularizers and mainstreamers of replacement theory.
sentences.zh: 直到今年，全国最受欢迎的有线电视主持人塔克·卡尔森（Tucker Carlson），也是置换理论的主要推广者和主流化者之一。

sentences.en: On his show, you could hear that rhetoric all the time,
sentences.zh: 在他的节目中，你经常能听到这种言论，

sentences.en: that Democrats in cahoots with big business and some Republicans were trying to replace the native-born population of America with immigrants for political power.
sentences.zh: 即民主党人与大企业及一些共和党人勾结，试图为了政治权力而用移民取代美国的本土出生人口。

sentences.en: And Elise Stefanik herself has delved into these waters.
sentences.zh: 埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克本人也曾涉足过这些领域。

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Two years ago, her campaign released Facebook ads that essentially borrowed and echoed elements of replacement theory.
sentences.zh: 两年前，她的竞选团队发布的Facebook广告在本质上借用了并呼应了“大置换理论”的要素。

sentences.en: She got bashed for this.
sentences.zh: 她因此遭到了抨击。

sentences.en: Of course, she was defiant.
sentences.zh: 当然，她表现得很不服气。

sentences.en: But it shows you how, if you think about all the discussion that replacement theory has caused in the media and on this show and around the country,
sentences.zh: 但这向你展示了，如果你回想一下媒体、本节目以及全国范围内围绕“大置换理论”所引发的所有讨论，

sentences.en: you can understand that this hearing was a chance to kind of flip the script and reset that conversation for Republicans and say, see, the real problem with anti-Semitism,
sentences.zh: 你就能明白，这次听证会对于共和党人来说是一个扭转局面、重塑对话的机会，他们想说：看吧，反犹主义的真正问题，

sentences.en: the real anti-Semites are at elite universities.
sentences.zh: 真正的反犹分子其实是在精英大学里。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: In other words, Republicans are very eager to redirect this conversation about anti-Semitism to being a problem of the left, not just the right.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，共和党人非常渴望将这场关于反犹主义的对话引向左派的问题，而不仅仅是右派的问题。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think we should also look at the broader context here.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们也应该看看这里更广泛的背景。

sentences.en: While the subject here is partly about who gets to say what, right?
sentences.zh: 虽然这里的主题部分涉及谁有权发表言论，对吧？

sentences.en: Should we have free speech?
sentences.zh: 我们应该拥有言论自由吗？

sentences.en: All around the country, in state legislatures, Republicans are passing bans on teaching critical race theory and defining that theory in pretty broad ways.
sentences.zh: 在全国各地的州议会中，共和党人正在通过禁令，禁止教授批判性种族理论，并对该理论进行了相当广泛的定义。

sentences.en: In Florida, professors are no longer allowed to talk about systemic racism in core classes.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州，教授们在核心课程中已不再被允许谈论系统性种族主义。

sentences.en: It's been banned.
sentences.zh: 它已经被禁了。

sentences.en: It's been banned.
sentences.zh: 它已经被禁了。

sentences.en: By Republican administration.
sentences.zh: 由共和党政府所禁。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so, you know, there are obviously a lot of principle defenders of free speech on the right and the left and in the center.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以，你知道，在右派、左派和中间派中显然有很多言论自由的原则捍卫者。

sentences.en: But I think some skepticism is warranted in this moment because rather than saying we should have more pluralism in these universities, we should accept all viewpoints.
sentences.zh: 但我认为此刻有必要保持一些怀疑态度，因为与其说我们应该在这些大学里实现更多的多元化、接受所有观点，

sentences.en: There are many people on the right at the right who want to replace one ideology with another.
sentences.zh: 右派中却有许多人想要用一种意识形态取代另一种意识形态。

sentences.en: Which is another way of saying that when it comes to academic free speech, there is some hypocrisy on both sides, not just on the left, but also on the right.
sentences.zh: 这换句话说就是，当谈到学术言论自由时，双方都存在某种虚伪，不仅仅是左派，右派也是如此。

sentences.en: I think there is an incredible amount of hypocrisy around free speech issues in every institution in American life.
sentences.zh: 我认为在美国生活的每一个机构中，围绕言论自由问题都存在着令人难以置信的虚伪。

sentences.en: Well, regardless of why Republicans seized on this moment and held this hearing, Nick,
sentences.zh: 好吧，尼克，无论共和党人为何抓住这个时机并举行这次听证会，

sentences.en: if you just embrace for the moment that universities are struggling with the question of free speech, when to embrace it, when to regulate it, I wonder where this now leads.
sentences.zh: 如果你暂时接受大学正在努力应对言论自由的问题——即何时拥护它、何时监管它——我很好奇这现在会导致什么结果。

sentences.en: Once a president of a university is ousted over this, once two other university presidents' jobs have been put on the line, even if they are spared, where do we think this goes?
sentences.zh: 一旦一位大学校长因此被赶下台，一旦另外两位大学校长的职位岌岌可危，即使他们幸免于难，你认为这会走向何方？

sentences.en: Does it lead to more free speech or does it lead to more regulation of free speech on these campuses?
sentences.zh: 这会导致更多的言论自由，还是会导致这些校园对言论自由进行更多的监管？

sentences.en: We have been moving in the direction of more regulation of campus speech for a long time now.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，我们一直朝着加强校园言论监管的方向发展。

sentences.en: I think for a long time, liberals led that charge, and I think that conservatives, some conservatives,
sentences.zh: 我认为长期以来，自由派主导了这一进程，而我认为保守派，一些保守派，

sentences.en: have given up on the idea of fighting for neutrality on these questions and have resolved that if there has to be a choice,
sentences.zh: 已经放弃了在这些问题上争取中立的想法，并下定决心，如果必须做出选择，

sentences.en: then they're going to enforce conservative speech restrictions and content restrictions on college campuses.
sentences.zh: 那么他们就要在大学校园里强制执行保守派的言论限制和内容限制。

sentences.en: Kind of match what's going on in their minds on the left.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是在与他们心目中左派的做法相抗衡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the other option for everybody is to make a decision as an institution, as a society, that we're going to be offended sometimes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对每个人来说，另一个选择是作为一个机构、作为一个社会做出决定：我们有时会感到被冒犯。

sentences.en: People are going to say things we don't like.
sentences.zh: 人们会说一些我们不喜欢的话。

sentences.en: They're going to lie.
sentences.zh: 他们会撒谎。

sentences.en: They're going to mislead.
sentences.zh: 他们会误导。

sentences.en: They're going to say, I shouldn't exiSt. They're going to be hateful.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我不应该存在。他们会充满仇恨。

sentences.en: And make a decision that maybe we have to let that happen and police it less.
sentences.zh: 并做出决定，也许我们必须让这种情况发生，并减少对它的监管。

sentences.en: Because that, in theory, is the true meaning of free speech, as painful as it clearly is.
sentences.zh: 因为从理论上讲，这就是言论自由的真正含义，尽管这显然很痛苦。

sentences.en: I think free speech is often painful.
sentences.zh: 我认为言论自由往往是痛苦的。

sentences.en: And we have worked away from that ideal in a lot of places in public life.
sentences.zh: 我们在公共生活的许多地方已经背离了这一理想。

sentences.en: But, you know, the idea that I'm going to have to be offended once in a while, even really offended, even feel that somebody is against who I am on some fundamental level,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，那种“我偶尔不得不被冒犯，甚至是非常被冒犯，甚至感到有人在某种根本层面上反对我的存在”的想法，

sentences.en: I think the choice that we all have to make is, is it better in the end to do less to regulate that kind of thing
sentences.zh: 我认为我们所有人都必须做出的选择是：最终，在监管这类事情上做得少一点，

sentences.en: and embrace all the pain and complexity that may result?
sentences.zh: 并拥抱可能由此产生的所有痛苦和复杂性，是否会更好？

sentences.en: And do we believe that that makes for a healthier society?
sentences.zh: 我们是否相信这会造就一个更健康的社会？

sentences.en: Based on what you're saying, it doesn't seem that's the direction we're headed in, towards a purer version of free speech on campus.
sentences.zh: 根据你所说的，我们似乎并没有朝着那个方向前进，即校园内更纯粹的言论自由版本。

sentences.en: It doesn't to me.
sentences.zh: 在我看来并没有。

sentences.en: And what I see is an expanding circle of things that you're not supposed to say in these environments.
sentences.zh: 我所看到的是，在这些环境中，你不应该说的话的范围正在扩大。

sentences.en: Not a shrinking one, but an expanding one.
sentences.zh: 不是在缩小，而是在扩大。

sentences.en: And it seems like that's the way we're heading.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来我们正朝着那个方向前进。

sentences.en: The notion that the administrations of these universities should try to remain neutral on moral and political questions and let everyone speak their perspective
sentences.zh: 那种认为这些大学的管理层应该在道德和政治问题上保持中立，并让每个人表达自己观点的观念，

sentences.en: seems less and less in favor.
sentences.zh: 似乎越来越不受欢迎了。

sentences.en: And it feels like we're moving more in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们正朝着相反的方向前进。

sentences.en: To a future in which in any given institution,
sentences.zh: 走向一个未来，在这个未来中，在任何给定的机构里，

sentences.en: whichever political side has the most power,
sentences.zh: 无论哪一方政治势力拥有最大的权力，

sentences.en: gets to decide what speech is really allowed.
sentences.zh: 都有权决定什么言论才是真正被允许的。

sentences.en: Well, Nick, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，尼克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 周二，拜登总统对他迄今为止在加沙的以色列军事战术提出了最强烈的批评，

sentences.zh: 他在那里请求尽快批准更多的军事援助，却遭到了国会共和党人的坚决抵制。

sentences.en: Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson said that members of his party had seen little evidence that Ukraine has a real plan to defeat Russia.
sentences.zh: 共和党众议院议长迈克·约翰逊表示，他所在党的成员几乎没有看到证据表明乌克兰有击败俄罗斯的真正计划。

sentences.en: I have asked the White House since the day that I was handed the gavel as speaker for clarity.
sentences.zh: 自从我接过议长木槌的那天起，我就一直要求白宫给出明确的说明。

sentences.en: We need a clear articulation of the strategy to allow Ukraine to win.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一个清晰的战略阐述，以使乌克兰能够获胜。

sentences.en: And thus far, their responses have been insufficient.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他们的回应还不够充分。

sentences.en: They have not provided...
sentences.zh: 他们还没有提供……

sentences.en: And that without such a plan, it doesn't make sense to keep giving Ukraine more money, as President Biden has requested.
sentences.zh: 而且如果没有这样的计划，继续按照拜登总统的要求向乌克兰提供更多资金是没有意义的。

sentences.en: And so what the Biden administration seems to be asking for is billions of additional dollars with no appropriate oversight, no clear strategy to win,
sentences.zh: 所以拜登政府似乎要求的是数十亿美元的额外资金，却没有适当的监督，没有明确的获胜战略，

sentences.en: and none of the answers that I think the American people are owed.
sentences.zh: 也没有我认为美国人民应得的任何答案。

sentences.en: Biden has warned that unless Congress approves more funding by the end of the year, which seems increasingly unlikely,

sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。
